rest.edge.answers.sessionRequired: `/bff/api/<path>`, any method, and the seller web's merchant socket under `/bff/ws/v1/matching/merchant`, when the browser sent no usable `__Host-kx_session`: none at all, a value that is not 43 base64url characters, or the cookie twice (a second copy must never decide which session is used). Nothing was forwarded. Sign in with `POST /bff/login`.
rest.edge.answers.sessionEnded: `/bff/api/<path>`, any method, and the seller web's merchant socket under `/bff/ws/v1/matching/merchant`, when `__Host-kx_session` names no live session: its idle or absolute limit passed, even while this request was being checked; it was signed out; a newer sign-in or sign-up in this browser replaced it; or identity refused to renew its tokens and the edge deleted it. Nothing was forwarded, and the cookie is expired. Sign in again.
rest.edge.answers.csrfRefused: Any `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` under `/bff/`, when the request does not come from the app's own page: `Origin` is present and is not exactly the origin the request came to (`https://seller.wildanfrananda.my.id` on the seller web; on the backoffice, `<backoffice origin>`, which is a different origin on its onion service and at its staff-network address, so each refuses the other's; the other app's origin and `null` are refused too), or `Origin` is absent and `Sec-Fetch-Site` is not `same-origin`. Checked before the session store or identity is asked: nothing was done and the session is untouched. A `fetch` from the app's own page passes; a page on another origin, a form posted from elsewhere, or a script outside a browser that sends neither header does not. The merchant socket's handshake is a `GET` and is checked too, more strictly: `Origin` must be present and exactly `https://seller.wildanfrananda.my.id`. Other `GET` and `HEAD` requests are never checked.
rest.edge.answers.roleRefused: `/bff/api/<path>` and the seller web's merchant socket under `/bff/ws/v1/matching/merchant`, when the edge renewed the access token and identity's answer carries a role this app does not admit: on the seller web the account is no longer `seller` or `customer` (a `customer` approved as a courier became `courier`), on the backoffice it is no longer `admin`. The session is deleted, the tokens just issued are signed out at identity, and the cookie is expired; nothing was forwarded. A `customer` approved as a seller is admitted and keeps the session. Sign-in and code verification list their own role refusal.
rest.edge.answers.notFound: Any path under `/bff/` that the edge does not serve on this host: anything but `/bff/session`, `/bff/login`, `/bff/logout`, the three `/bff/2fa/` endpoints and `/bff/api/<path>` on both hosts, and `/bff/register` and the merchant socket's two paths (`/bff/ws/v1/matching/merchant`, and the same followed by `/websocket`) on the seller web only; on the backoffice those three get this answer with the method they take. `/bff/api` without a path after it gets this answer too. A path outside `/bff/` on the two app hosts never reaches the edge: Kong answers it.
rest.edge.answers.refusedPath: `/bff/api/<path>` when the path is one of identity's token-issuing routes, or under one, in any letter case and even percent-encoded: `/api/v1/auth/login`, `/api/v1/auth/register`, `/api/v1/auth/refresh`, `/api/v1/auth/logout`, `/api/v1/auth/2fa/verify`, `/api/v1/auth/2fa/passkey/verify` and `/api/v1/couriers/register`. Their answers would hand a token to JavaScript. Sign up (on the seller web), sign in, verify and sign out with the edge's own endpoints; the edge renews tokens by itself; a courier account cannot be registered through the edge. Refused before the session is read: nothing was forwarded.
rest.edge.answers.methodNotAllowed: A path the edge serves, with a method it does not take: `/bff/session` and the merchant socket's paths take `GET`; `/bff/login`, `/bff/register`, `/bff/logout` and the three `/bff/2fa/` endpoints take `POST`; `/bff/api/<path>` takes `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE`. `Allow` lists them for the path asked. The method is checked before the host, so on the backoffice a wrong method on `/bff/register` or a socket path gets this answer rather than `404`. An `OPTIONS` gets this answer too: the edge answers no CORS, because the app and the edge share an origin.
rest.edge.answers.payloadTooLarge: Any request under `/bff/` whose body is larger than 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes), refused by the edge's web server before anything else. Kong passes such a body on, so this is the answer a browser gets. `requestId` here is the edge's own 32-character id, not the `X-Request-Id` of the request.
rest.edge.answers.uriTooLong: A request line longer than 8 KiB (8,192 bytes), in practice a very long query string. Kong's own limit is the same size, so Kong usually refuses such a request first, with its own answer. `requestId` here is the edge's own 32-character id.
rest.edge.answers.jsonRequired: Any `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` under `/bff/` that carries a body (a `Content-Length` other than `0`, or `Transfer-Encoding`) whose `Content-Type` is not `application/json`; parameters such as `charset` are allowed. Checked right after the origin, before anything else: nothing was done. A request without a body needs no `Content-Type`. HTML forms and `multipart/form-data` cannot go through the edge.
rest.edge.answers.headersTooLarge: Request headers too large for the edge's web server: one header line (a long `Cookie` included) over 8 KiB, or all of them together over about 32 KiB. Kong's limits are the same size, so Kong usually refuses such a request first. `requestId` here is the edge's own 32-character id.
rest.edge.answers.internal: Any request under `/bff/`, when something fails in the edge that it did not expect. Whether the request took effect is not known: read the current state (`GET /bff/session`, or the resource) before retrying.
rest.edge.answers.identityFailed: `POST /bff/login`, `POST /bff/register`, the three `/bff/2fa/` endpoints and `POST /bff/logout`, when identity answers in a way the edge does not understand: a status or a body it does not expect, or a refusal of the app's own client name, which is a configuration fault on Kinetix's side. No cookie changed and a session the browser had is kept. Retry later.
rest.edge.answers.storeUnavailable: Any request under `/bff/` except one refused earlier (origin, body, path, method), when the edge cannot reach its session store, or the store refuses a read or a write. The edge never falls back to anything, and no cookie changed. A sign-in or sign-up is refused before identity is asked, so it does not count against the account and creates nothing; only if the store fails after identity answered are the tokens identity issued signed out, and an account a sign-up created stays (`POST /bff/register` tells how to go on). A sign-out keeps the session, unless identity has already ended it: then the answer is `204`. `/bff/api/<path>` and the merchant socket forward nothing. Retry later.
rest.edge.answers.identityUnavailable: `POST /bff/login`, `POST /bff/register` and the three `/bff/2fa/` endpoints, when identity cannot be reached or answers with a `5xx`: the edge kept nothing (a sign-up that got no answer may still have created the account, see `POST /bff/register`). `/bff/api/<path>`, the merchant socket and `POST /bff/logout`, when the access token has under 60 seconds left and the edge cannot renew it now: identity unreachable, a `5xx`, identity's own rate limit, or another request of the same session renewing it did not finish within 9 seconds. The session is kept in every case; retry later.
rest.edge.answers.apiUnavailable: `/bff/api/<path>`, when the edge cannot reach the API (the gateway, or identity itself for `/api/v1/auth/...` and `/api/v1/couriers/...`), or gets no answer within 60 seconds. The request may have reached the service: read the current state before retrying, or retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` where the endpoint takes one. Also the seller web's merchant socket, when the edge cannot reach the gateway or gets no answer to the handshake within 90 seconds: no socket was opened, and connecting again is safe. A service that is down behind a gateway that answers does not give this answer: Kong's own `502`, `503` or `504` is passed on with its status and body, on `/bff/api/<path>` and on the socket alike (see Kong's answers).
rest.edge.session.summary: Tells the page whether this browser is signed in to this app, with which role and principal, and until when. It never answers a token.
rest.edge.session.who: Anyone on the app's host, with or without `__Host-kx_session`. The backoffice admits `admin` accounts only, each with two-factor authentication; the seller web admits `seller` and `customer`. On the backoffice host, only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers.
rest.edge.session.case.signedIn: The session is live. `role` is the role at sign-in or at the edge's latest renewal of the tokens, so a role granted since then shows only after a `/bff/api/` call has renewed them (when the access token is under 60 seconds from expiry). `expiresAt` is when the session ends if it is not used: the idle limit from the last `/bff/api/` call, capped by the absolute limit — 15 minutes and 8 hours on the backoffice, 7 days and 30 days on the seller web. Reading this endpoint is not a use: it neither extends the session nor renews its tokens, so polling it keeps nothing alive.
rest.edge.session.case.anonymous: The browser sent no usable `__Host-kx_session`: none, a malformed value, or the cookie twice. Show the sign-in.
rest.edge.session.case.ended: `__Host-kx_session` is well formed but names no live session: it ended by its idle or absolute limit, a sign-out, a newer sign-in or sign-up, or a refused renewal. The answer expires the cookie. Show the sign-in.
rest.edge.login.summary: Signs in to this app with an email and a password. Answers a session behind an `HttpOnly` cookie, or a sign-in that still needs a second factor (`mfaRequired`, on the backoffice with `passkeys`), or, on the backoffice, the enrolment of a second factor (`mfaEnrolmentRequired`). No token reaches the page.
rest.edge.login.who: Anyone on the app's host; no cookie is needed. The backoffice admits `admin` accounts only, and leads an admin without two-factor authentication through enrolment first; the seller web admits `seller` and `customer` (an applicant signs in as a `customer`). On the backoffice host, only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers.
rest.edge.login.field.email: A string of 1 to 254 characters; identity then requires a valid email address and matches it without regard to case.
rest.edge.login.field.password: A string of 1 to 1,024 characters; identity requires at least 6. The edge passes only `email` and `password` on and ignores any other field.
rest.edge.login.case.session: Seller web only: the password is right, the account has no second factor, and its role is `seller` or `customer`. A new session starts behind `__Host-kx_session`, whose `Max-Age` is the 30-day absolute limit, so it survives a browser restart; the session ends after 7 days without a `/bff/api/` call, or 30 days after sign-in. A session the browser already had on this host is deleted, its tokens are signed out at identity, and a session with a new id replaces it. On the backoffice a password alone never starts a session: every `admin` has two-factor authentication, or is led to enrol.
rest.edge.login.case.challenge: Seller web: the password is right and the account has two-factor authentication on, as any seller may turn it on. The answer is `mfaRequired` alone, whether or not the account holds a passkey: the seller web offers none. No session yet: identity's challenge stays in the edge behind `__Host-kx_pending`, for identity's 300 seconds. Send the authenticator's code to `POST /bff/2fa/verify` within that time. A pending sign-in the browser already had is replaced.
rest.edge.login.case.challengeBackoffice: Backoffice: the password is right and the account has two-factor authentication on, as every `admin` has once enrolled. `passkeys` is `true` when the account holds a passkey: the page may then offer it beside the code, through `POST /bff/2fa/passkey/options` and `POST /bff/2fa/passkey/verify`. The code always works, at `POST /bff/2fa/verify`. No session yet: identity's challenge stays in the edge behind `__Host-kx_pending`, for identity's 300 seconds. A pending sign-in the browser already had is replaced.
rest.edge.login.case.enrolment: Backoffice only: the password is right and the account is an `admin` with no second factor yet. No session: the enrolment stays in the edge behind `__Host-kx_pending` for 600 seconds. Call `POST /bff/2fa/setup` to get the secret to show, then `POST /bff/2fa/enable` with a code from it, then sign in again.
rest.edge.login.case.invalid: The body is not a JSON object with `email` and `password` as non-empty strings within their limits (identity was not asked), or identity refused them: `email` not a valid address, or `password` shorter than 6 characters. Nothing was kept; correct the fields and send again.
rest.edge.login.case.wrongCredentials: No account has this email, or the password is wrong; identity answers both alike. The attempt counts towards identity's delay for this account (`SIGN_IN_DELAYED`).
rest.edge.login.case.roleRefused: The password is right, but this app does not admit the account's role: anything but `admin` on the backoffice; `courier` or `admin` on the seller web. The tokens identity just issued are signed out at identity at once, so no session exists anywhere and no session cookie is set; a `__Host-kx_pending` sent along is expired. An `admin` without a second factor is refused on the seller web as soon as identity asks for enrolment. An account with two-factor authentication on gets `mfaRequired` first and is refused at `POST /bff/2fa/verify` or `POST /bff/2fa/passkey/verify`, because its role is known only once the second factor is right.
rest.edge.login.case.delayed: identity is holding back sign-ins to this account: from the fifth attempt that has not ended in a sign-in (a password or a code; the count is forgotten an hour after the last one), each attempt must wait 1 second after the previous one, doubling up to 60 seconds. Nothing was checked. Wait the seconds in `Retry-After`, then try again; a completed sign-in clears the count.
rest.edge.login.case.throttled: More than 5 sign-in attempts from this browser's address within 60 seconds, identity's limit. The edge passes identity the browser's address alone, so each address has its own count. Nothing was checked; wait the seconds in `Retry-After`, sent when identity gives them.
rest.edge.register.summary: Creates a Kinetix account from the seller web with an email and a password, and signs the browser in at once: the account is a `customer`, and the answer starts its session behind an `HttpOnly` cookie, as a sign-in does. No token reaches the page.
rest.edge.register.who: Anyone on the seller web's host, `seller.wildanfrananda.my.id`; no cookie is needed. The backoffice does not offer it: there the edge answers `404` `NOT_FOUND` without asking identity. Every new account is a `customer`, which the seller web admits; selling needs an application an admin approves.
rest.edge.register.field.email: A string of 1 to 254 characters; identity then requires a valid email address of at most 254 characters and stores it in lower case, so addresses that differ only in case are the same account.
rest.edge.register.field.password: A string of 1 to 1,024 characters; identity requires at least 12 characters and at most 72 bytes in UTF-8. The edge passes only `email` and `password` on and ignores any other field.
rest.edge.register.case.created: identity created the account as a `customer` and signed it in. A new session starts behind `__Host-kx_session` as after a sign-in on the seller web: `Max-Age` of 30 days, and the session ends after 7 days without a `/bff/api/` call, or 30 days after sign-up. A session the browser already had on this host is deleted, its tokens are signed out at identity, and a `__Host-kx_pending` sent along is expired. The account has no second factor, so no code is asked: the page goes on signed in.
rest.edge.register.case.invalid: The body is not a JSON object with `email` and `password` as non-empty strings within the edge's limits. identity was not asked and nothing was created; correct the fields and send again.
rest.edge.register.case.rejected: identity refused the values: `email` is not a valid address, or `password` is shorter than 12 characters or longer than 72 bytes. `message` carries identity's own words, every rule that failed joined by semicolons, ready to show beside the form; it is the edge's general message when identity's is missing or longer than 500 characters. Nothing was created.
rest.edge.register.case.emailTaken: An account with this email already exists, in any letter case. Nothing was created. Sign in with `POST /bff/login` instead. A retry after a `503` gets this answer when the first attempt had created the account before the failure: sign in then.
rest.edge.register.case.throttled: More than 5 sign-ups from this browser's address within 60 seconds, identity's limit. The edge passes identity the browser's address alone, so each address has its own count. Nothing was created; wait the seconds in `Retry-After`, sent when identity gives them.
rest.edge.verifyTwoFactor.summary: Completes a sign-in that answered `mfaRequired`: has identity check the authenticator's code, then starts the session.
rest.edge.verifyTwoFactor.who: A browser holding `__Host-kx_pending` from a sign-in on the same host that answered `mfaRequired`. The account's role is checked here, after the code: the backoffice admits `admin`, the seller web `seller` and `customer`. On the backoffice host, only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers.
rest.edge.verifyTwoFactor.field.code: The six digits the authenticator app shows now. The edge takes a string of 1 to 16 characters and passes it on; identity accepts six digits, spaces around them ignored, and a code from the 30 seconds before or after as well. Each code works once.
rest.edge.verifyTwoFactor.case.sessionBa: Backoffice: the code is right and the account is an `admin`. The session starts behind `__Host-kx_session` with no `Max-Age`, so the cookie ends when the browser closes; the session ends after 15 minutes without a `/bff/api/` call, or 8 hours after sign-in. `__Host-kx_pending` is expired.
rest.edge.verifyTwoFactor.case.sessionSe: Seller web: the code is right and the role is `seller` or `customer`. The session starts as after a sign-in without a code: `__Host-kx_session` with `Max-Age` of 30 days, 7 days idle at most. `__Host-kx_pending` is expired.
rest.edge.verifyTwoFactor.case.invalid: The body is not a JSON object with `code` as a string of 1 to 16 characters (neither the store nor identity was asked), or identity refused the code's form: not six digits. The pending sign-in is kept; send a six-digit code.
rest.edge.verifyTwoFactor.case.codeRefus: identity refused the code: it is neither the authenticator's current code nor one from the 30 seconds before or after. The pending sign-in is kept, so the next code can be sent. A challenge takes five codes at most: after the fifth, the next one answers `SIGN_IN_REQUIRED`.
rest.edge.verifyTwoFactor.case.signInReq: No pending challenge: `__Host-kx_pending` is missing or malformed, its 300 seconds have passed, it was already used, it was started on the other app, or it holds an enrolment, which cannot answer a challenge (trying ends it). identity was not asked. A pending cookie that was sent is expired. Sign in again with `POST /bff/login`.
rest.edge.verifyTwoFactor.case.challenge: identity ended the challenge: five codes were already tried on it; it was already answered, from another tab for instance; the code had already been used for a sign-in moments before, which spends the challenge; or identity no longer accepts it, because it expired or the account no longer has two-factor authentication or no longer exists. The edge deletes the pending sign-in and expires `__Host-kx_pending`. Sign in again with `POST /bff/login`, then send the code the authenticator shows next.
rest.edge.verifyTwoFactor.case.roleRefus: The code is right, but this app does not admit the account's role: an `admin` on the seller web, any other role on the backoffice. The tokens are signed out at identity at once, no session starts, and `__Host-kx_pending` is expired.
rest.edge.verifyTwoFactor.case.delayed: identity is holding back sign-ins to this account after repeated attempts, as at sign-in. Nothing was checked and the pending sign-in is kept. Wait the seconds in `Retry-After`, then send the code that is current then.
rest.edge.verifyTwoFactor.case.throttled: More than 5 codes from this browser's address within 60 seconds, identity's limit. Nothing was checked and the pending sign-in is kept; wait the seconds in `Retry-After`, sent when identity gives them.
rest.edge.passkeyOptions.summary: Backoffice only: asks identity for the WebAuthn request options with which one of the admin's passkeys answers the pending challenge, instead of a code. Pass `options` to `navigator.credentials.get()`, then send its answer to `POST /bff/2fa/passkey/verify`.
rest.edge.passkeyOptions.who: A browser on the backoffice holding `__Host-kx_pending` from a sign-in that answered `mfaRequired` with `passkeys: true`. The request needs no body. The seller web does not serve this path.
rest.edge.passkeyOptions.case.options: identity's options, passed on unchanged: the account's passkeys in `allowCredentials`, user verification required, 120 seconds. The challenge token stays in the edge, and the pending sign-in is kept; asking again replaces the options.
rest.edge.passkeyOptions.case.passkeyRef: The account holds no passkey any more: it was removed after the sign-in answered `passkeys: true`. The pending sign-in is kept: answer it with the code at `POST /bff/2fa/verify`.
rest.edge.passkeyOptions.case.signInRequ: No pending challenge: `__Host-kx_pending` is missing or malformed, its 300 seconds have passed, it was already used, it was started on another app, or it holds an enrolment, which cannot answer a challenge (trying ends it). identity was not asked. A pending cookie that was sent is expired. Sign in again with `POST /bff/login`.
rest.edge.passkeyOptions.case.challengeE: identity ended the challenge: it was already answered, from another tab for instance, or identity no longer accepts it, because it expired or the account no longer has two-factor authentication or no longer exists. The edge deletes the pending sign-in and expires `__Host-kx_pending`. Sign in again with `POST /bff/login`.
rest.edge.passkeyOptions.case.notOffered: Seller web: it offers no passkeys, so the path is not served. Nothing was read, and a pending sign-in is kept for the code.
rest.edge.passkeyOptions.case.throttled: More than 5 requests from this browser's address within 60 seconds, identity's limit. Nothing was checked and the pending sign-in is kept; wait the seconds in `Retry-After`, sent when identity gives them.
rest.edge.verifyPasskey.summary: Backoffice only: completes a sign-in that answered `mfaRequired` with a passkey instead of a code. Has identity check the browser's answer to the options of `POST /bff/2fa/passkey/options`, then starts the session exactly as `POST /bff/2fa/verify` does.
rest.edge.verifyPasskey.who: A browser on the backoffice holding `__Host-kx_pending` from a sign-in that answered `mfaRequired`. The account's role is checked here, after the passkey: the backoffice admits `admin` only. The seller web does not serve this path.
rest.edge.verifyPasskey.field.credential: The object `navigator.credentials.get()` resolved to, as JSON, with every binary value in base64url. The edge takes a JSON object in a body of at most 16 KiB and passes it to identity unchanged.
rest.edge.verifyPasskey.case.session: The passkey is one of the admin's and its answer verifies. The session starts exactly as after a code: `__Host-kx_session` with no `Max-Age`, so the cookie ends when the browser closes; the session ends after 15 minutes without a `/bff/api/` call, or 8 hours after sign-in. `__Host-kx_pending` is expired.
rest.edge.verifyPasskey.case.invalid: The body is not a JSON object whose `credential` is a JSON object, or is larger than 16 KiB (neither the store nor identity was asked), or identity refused the body's form. The pending sign-in is kept.
rest.edge.verifyPasskey.case.passkeyRefu: identity refused the passkey: it is not one of the account's, its answer does not verify, its counter went back, or the options it answers were replaced or are older than 120 seconds. The pending sign-in is kept: ask for new options and try again, or send the code to `POST /bff/2fa/verify`. A challenge takes five answers at most, passkeys and codes together: after the fifth, the next one answers `SIGN_IN_REQUIRED`.
rest.edge.verifyPasskey.case.signInRequi: No pending challenge: `__Host-kx_pending` is missing or malformed, its 300 seconds have passed, it was already used, it was started on another app, or it holds an enrolment, which cannot answer a challenge (trying ends it). identity was not asked. A pending cookie that was sent is expired. Sign in again with `POST /bff/login`.
rest.edge.verifyPasskey.case.challengeEn: identity ended the challenge: five answers were already tried on it; it was already answered, from another tab for instance, or the same passkey signed another sign-in at the same moment; or identity no longer accepts it, because it expired or the account no longer has two-factor authentication or no longer exists. The edge deletes the pending sign-in and expires `__Host-kx_pending`. Sign in again with `POST /bff/login`.
rest.edge.verifyPasskey.case.roleRefused: The passkey is right, but the account is not an `admin`. The tokens are signed out at identity at once, no session starts, and `__Host-kx_pending` is expired.
rest.edge.verifyPasskey.case.notOffered: Seller web: it offers no passkeys, so the path is not served. Nothing was read, and a pending sign-in is kept for the code.
rest.edge.verifyPasskey.case.delayed: identity is holding back sign-ins to this account after repeated attempts, as at sign-in. Nothing was checked, and the pending sign-in and its options are kept. Wait the seconds in `Retry-After`, then send the answer again while the options' 120 seconds last.
rest.edge.verifyPasskey.case.throttled: More than 5 answers from this browser's address within 60 seconds, identity's limit. Nothing was checked and the pending sign-in is kept; wait the seconds in `Retry-After`, sent when identity gives them.
rest.edge.setupTwoFactor.summary: First step of an admin's enrolment in two-factor authentication: answers a new secret for the authenticator app, as text and as an `otpauth://` URL to show as a QR code.
rest.edge.setupTwoFactor.who: A browser holding `__Host-kx_pending` from a backoffice sign-in that answered `mfaEnrolmentRequired`: an `admin` without a second factor. The seller web never gets here, since it admits no `admin`. Only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers.
rest.edge.setupTwoFactor.case.secret: The enrolment is current. identity generated a new secret and keeps it, not yet active, until `POST /bff/2fa/enable` confirms it. Show `qrCodeUrl` as a QR code, and `twoFactorSecret` for typing in by hand, then ask for a code. Calling this again replaces the secret, so only codes from the latest one are accepted. A request body, if any, is ignored; no cookie changes.
rest.edge.setupTwoFactor.case.signInRequ: No pending enrolment: `__Host-kx_pending` is missing or malformed, its 600 seconds have passed, it was started on the other app, it holds a challenge instead (trying ends it), or identity no longer accepts the enrolment. A pending cookie that was sent is expired. Sign in again with `POST /bff/login`.
rest.edge.setupTwoFactor.case.alreadyEna: Two-factor authentication was turned on for this account after this enrolment began, through another sign-in. Nothing was changed. Sign in again: the next sign-in asks for a code.
rest.edge.setupTwoFactor.case.throttled: More than 5 setup calls from this browser's address within 60 seconds, identity's limit. Nothing was changed; wait the seconds in `Retry-After`, sent when identity gives them.
rest.edge.enableTwoFactor.summary: Second step of the enrolment: confirms a code from the new secret and turns two-factor authentication on. It starts no session; the admin then signs in again.
rest.edge.enableTwoFactor.who: A browser holding `__Host-kx_pending` from a backoffice sign-in that answered `mfaEnrolmentRequired`, after `POST /bff/2fa/setup`. Only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers.
rest.edge.enableTwoFactor.field.code: The six digits the authenticator app shows for the secret of the latest `POST /bff/2fa/setup`. The edge takes a string of 1 to 16 characters and passes it on; identity accepts six digits, spaces around them ignored. Each code works once.
rest.edge.enableTwoFactor.case.enabled: The code matches the latest secret. Two-factor authentication is on, every session the account had is ended at identity, and the enrolment is spent: `__Host-kx_pending` is expired and no session starts. Sign in again with `POST /bff/login`; it now answers `mfaRequired`.
rest.edge.enableTwoFactor.case.invalid: The body is not a JSON object with `code` as a string of 1 to 16 characters, or identity refused it: `code` not six digits, or no secret was set up yet (call `POST /bff/2fa/setup` first). The enrolment is kept.
rest.edge.enableTwoFactor.case.codeRefus: identity refused the code: it does not match the latest secret at this time, or it was already used. The enrolment is kept; send the next code.
rest.edge.enableTwoFactor.case.signInReq: No pending enrolment: `__Host-kx_pending` is missing or malformed, its 600 seconds have passed, it was started on the other app, it holds a challenge instead (trying ends it), or identity no longer accepts the enrolment. A pending cookie that was sent is expired. Sign in again with `POST /bff/login`.
rest.edge.enableTwoFactor.case.delayed: identity is holding back sign-ins to this account after repeated attempts, as at sign-in: each code sent here counts as an attempt. Nothing was checked and the enrolment is kept. Wait the seconds in `Retry-After`.
rest.edge.enableTwoFactor.case.throttled: More than 5 calls from this browser's address within 60 seconds, identity's limit. Nothing was checked and the enrolment is kept; wait the seconds in `Retry-After`, sent when identity gives them.
rest.edge.logout.summary: Signs out of this app: ends the session at identity and in the edge, and expires both cookies.
rest.edge.logout.who: Anyone on the app's host, with or without `__Host-kx_session`; any role the app admits (backoffice: `admin`; seller web: `seller` and `customer`). On the backoffice host, only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers.
rest.edge.logout.case.signedOut: The session's access token is revoked at identity, its refresh tokens can no longer be used, the edge deletes it, and both cookies are expired; a pending sign-in is dropped too. The edge first renews the access token when it has under 60 seconds left, so identity accepts the call. For a live session this answer comes only once identity has ended it, and then even if the edge's session store fails afterwards. The same answer comes when there was nothing to end: no cookie, or one whose session had already ended. Sign-out is safe to repeat.
rest.edge.logout.case.identityUnavailabl: identity could not be told: unreachable, a `5xx`, or its rate limit; or the access token needed a renewal identity could not give now. The session is kept and the browser is still signed in: retry the sign-out later. The edge never answers `204` for a live session without identity having ended it; an answer from identity it does not understand is `502` `IDENTITY_FAILED`, and the session is kept then too.
